title: Recipe Scaling and Unit Normalization
instructions:
Implement `units.py` and `recipes.py` for scaling and combining recipe ingredients. Use
exact rational arithmetic internally, then round only final output amounts.

In `units.py`:
- `parse_amount(value: int | float | str) -> fractions.Fraction`: accept nonnegative finite
  ints/floats (exclude bool), converting floats through their decimal string. Strings are
  stripped of outer whitespace and must be one of: digits (`'2'`), digits-dot-digits
  (`'2.50'`), integer fraction (`'3/4'`), or mixed fraction (`'1 1/2'`, exactly one space).
  All components are unsigned decimal ASCII digits. Leading zeroes are allowed. A mixed
  fraction is whole + numerator/denominator; improper fractions are allowed. Zero
  denominators, negative values, signs, exponent strings, `.5`, `2.`, internal extra
  whitespace, invalid types and malformed strings raise `ValueError`.
- `normalize_unit(unit: str) -> tuple[str, int]`: strip whitespace, lowercase, and return
  (canonical unit, multiplier). Unknown units raise `ValueError`. Accept ONLY these groups:
  `g/gram/grams` -> ('g',1); `kg/kilogram/kilograms` -> ('g',1000);
  `ml/milliliter/milliliters` -> ('ml',1); `l/liter/liters` -> ('ml',1000);
  `tsp/teaspoon/teaspoons` -> ('ml',5); `tbsp/tablespoon/tablespoons` -> ('ml',15);
  `cup/cups` -> ('ml',240); `each/piece/pieces` -> ('each',1).
  Unit inputs are strings.

In `recipes.py`, `scale_recipe(ingredients, servings, target_servings) -> list[dict]`:
- ingredients is any iterable of dicts with keys `name` (string), `amount`, `unit` (string).
  No validation of the dict structure is needed. Parse amounts with parse_amount.
- Parse both serving counts with parse_amount, additionally requiring both > 0, else
  `ValueError`. Multiply each ingredient by target_servings / servings and its unit factor.
- Strip and lowercase names; empty names raise `ValueError`. Preserve internal spaces.
- Combine items with the same normalized name AND canonical unit. The same name in
  different unit families remains separate. Keep groups in first-appearance order, including
  zero-amount groups. Each result has exactly `name`, `amount`, `unit`; amount is a float
  produced by `float(round(total_fraction, 6))` (ties to even). No other rounding occurs.
- Never mutate input records. Propagate helper validation errors. Even an empty recipe
  validates both serving counts and then returns [].
Numeric inputs in tests are small enough for ordinary float output.

## Files
- `units.py`
- `recipes.py`
